subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class cron-scoped hard tool policy, and if so should it be `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, inheritance from `tools.subagents.tools`, or part of the broader per-session policy design?
rationale: The missing behavior requires a new public config/security boundary and precedence rules; current per-job `toolsAllow` is not a replacement for an operator-wide deny policy.

options.title: Design cron policy in session-policy model
options.body: Use the broader per-session/capability-policy direction to define cron precedence first, then add one canonical cron enforcement path with docs and tests.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron sessions as inheriting `tools.subagents.tools` where safe, reducing config surface but coupling two different runtime classes.

options.title: Fold into session policy
options.body: Keep this open under the broader per-session tool-policy design and avoid a standalone cron key until that RFC settles.

recommendation.title: Design cron policy in session-policy model
recommendation.body: Use the broader per-session/capability-policy direction to define cron precedence first, then add one canonical cron enforcement path with docs and tests.
